answer: Operator Liability Anchor. Each identity registers with a persistent operator key, not just a wallet. A lantern flag on that key triggers a graduated clawback: when any one operator key exceeds a small cap of identities, every identity under it is throttled and a penalty is charged to the operator's shared settlement balance at the wharf, the payout address all its identities draw from. Attacker cost: one penalty per identity at the cap, plus loss of the payout channel, so spinning up N identities costs N times the settlement fee.
